geographyNote: County of Brant, Ontario (single-tier municipality; census subdivision Brant, City); excludes the separate City of Brantford

facts.text: The County of Brant issued more than $160 million in industrial and commercial permits in 2025, a record-breaking year for development.
facts.evidence: 2025 marked a record-breaking year for industrial and commercial development, with more than $160 million in permits issued and several major private-sector investments expected to create hundreds of jobs.

facts.text: Amazon plans a 200,000-square-foot last-mile delivery station near Rest Acres Road and Highway 403 in the County of Brant.
facts.evidence: Amazon's planned 200,000-square-foot last-mile delivery station near Rest Acres Road and Highway 403, as well as the relocation of 1200 Degrees Ontario to Burford. These investments, along with Tigercat, are expected to create approximately 400 jobs.

facts.text: Tigercat Industries continues to expand in Paris, including completion of a new 275,000-square-foot facility.
facts.evidence: Tigercat Industries' continued expansion in Paris, including completion of a new 275,000-square-foot facility.

facts.text: The County of Brant targets heavy manufacturing, advanced manufacturing, and warehousing and logistics for investment.
facts.evidence: The County of Brant has focused on attracting industries that suit its location and workforce, including heavy manufacturing, advanced manufacturing, and warehousing and logistics.

meta.descriptor: a largely rural county surrounding Brantford, centred on the town of Paris
meta.fact: home to Tigercat Industries' expanding Paris operations and a planned Amazon delivery station

overview: The County of Brant had 39,474 residents in 2021, up 10.8% from 35,640 in 2016, living in 14,330 occupied private dwellings over 817.66 square kilometres. Customers are spread between Paris, smaller villages and farms, so few businesses can rely on walk-in traffic alone.

Record industrial investment, including new manufacturing and logistics facilities, is bringing more jobs and more households. Local businesses also compete with firms in Brantford, which sits right next door.

byService.lead-generation: With the County of Brant growing 10.8% since 2016 and new plants hiring, lead generation should target newcomers and young families settling around Paris and St. George.
byService.seo: County of Brant searches are split by village, so SEO should name Paris, St. George and Burford directly and also capture nearby Brantford queries.
byService.website-development: Across 817.66 square kilometres, a Brant website should state which villages a business serves and offer online booking so rural customers can act without calling.
byService.branding: Branding in the County of Brant can balance small-town heritage with growth, presenting a business as rooted in Paris or Burford yet ready for a busier county.
